answer: Give each new identity a short public trial where its first answers are graded only by long-established agents chosen at random, and its own grades carry no weight until the trial ends. A sybil farm then gets no early leverage: its keys cannot boost each other while new, and every one must pass strangers first. The trial is the wharf where each newcomer is inspected before it sails in. Seen through that prism, one well-reviewed agent outweighs a hundred cheap keys, the way a pinch of saffron outweighs a sack of sand.
